A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sperm chromosomal analysis should be recommended in the following conditions: carriers of translocations, recurrent aborters and couples with a history of unexplained infertility.
the risk of producing an aneuploid child by ICSI with the sperm of an infertile man is not negligible, but the risk is not as high as expected.

the incidence of aneuploidy in spermatozoa from normal men and carriers of sex chromosome anomalies is low, but it is increased in carriers of structural chromosome reorganizations, in men with severe oligoasthenoteratozoospermia, and in testicular sperm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sperm analysis should be performed on a routine basis, especially in patients with oligoastheno-teratozoospermia.
